metadata.description: Hatsu — the local plane of the Akatsuki system, and the way of working itself. Kurapika (/kurapika) leads in six declared Nen-type work-modes, named per reply; Gon, Hisoka, Phinks, Uvogin, Feitan and Chrollo stand beside him as ratified independents, and Illumi is provisioned — not ratified — for the long landing watch. Thirty-eight skills at v0.6.0: seventeen drive backlogs, PRs, releases and QA on deterministic Nen verbs (drive is renamed sharingan), and twenty-one are the way of working — breath, rasengan, kokusen, amaterasu, tsukuyomi, rikugan, jutaisho, ao, aka and ren for the local loop, the PR side added at v0.5.0 (hanten, gyo, kotoamatsukami, shibari, jujutsu, murasaki, mukai and en), and the release side new at v0.6.0: susanoo packages locally, kagutsuchi uploads to a non-production target on your own per-target call, and mugetsu publishes at G3. Two config files hold every parameter, two harness hooks ring the bell and refuse a commit on the trunk, and all five phases that stay yours to call now have skills. Runs on your own credentials — no App, no bot identity. Hard dependency on the Nen CLI, checked at warm-up and failing closed with auto-install.

plugins.description: Hatsu — the local plane of the Akatsuki system, and the way of working itself. Kurapika (/kurapika) leads in six declared Nen-type work-modes, named per reply — Enhancer (product code), Conjurer (canon & governance), Transmuter (machinery), Manipulator (GitHub-side ops), Emitter (release & fan-out), Specialist (product intake). Gon is the mission-scoped delegate who crosses no gate until his delegation grammar is ratified; Hisoka reviews UI/UX and measures quality before a PR posts; Phinks runs adversarial QA on proven findings, pre-release and now pre-PR on a release-adjacent change set; Uvogin measures the fixed seven performance metrics with method blocks and baselines; Feitan reviews security and security only — auth flows, secrets, network and storage boundaries, data minimisation — citing SEC-{n} by id; Chrollo reviews architecture and handbook conformance and never authors a handbook. Feitan and Chrollo were activated from the bench on 2026-09-09 and their definitions land at v0.5.0. Illumi is PROVISIONED, not ratified, for en's long watch alone — read-only, waking Kurapika and acting on nothing; Killua, the rest of Illumi's row and the five remaining bench profiles are recorded OPEN. Thirty-eight skills ship aboard. Seventeen answer a request — backlog-state, backlog-board, backlog-loop, backlog-synthesis, bankai-handbooks, bankai-quality, build, file, futon, getsuga, izanagi, izanami, jujisho, pr-state, senkei, sharingan (renamed from drive), tensho. Twenty-one are the way of working: breath (warm-up and the branch), rasengan (build before every commit), kokusen (commit, with an ask on every flagged file), amaterasu (launch from your own working directory), tsukuyomi (tests), rikugan (the rich HTML report), jutaisho (the bell), ao (pull from the base), aka (push — yours to call), ren (the per-request loop, which never pushes), and the PR side new at v0.5.0 — hanten (adversarial review, routed by scope), gyo (the coverage ladder), kotoamatsukami (UI tests), shibari (opens the one PR), jujutsu (device pairing), murasaki (pull + push), mukai (the review-and-PR phase, yours to call) and en (the capped landing watch) — and the release side new at v0.6.0: susanoo (the declared archive, run locally, uploading nothing), kagutsuchi (a non-production deploy or upload, yours to call, per target, the plan always printed and --run only on a call naming the target) and mugetsu (publication, yours to call, per target, at G3). With those three, four of the five phases only you may call have a skill — the fifth, the merge, has none, because G2 is an action no agent performs — and neither of the last two is ever reached from a composite. Every deterministic step is a Nen verb, with per-skill evidence in docs/ab/. Policy lives in nen/workflow.json and execution in nen/contract.json's project block (docs/WORKFLOW.md explains both); hooks/hooks.json rings the stop bell and refuses a commit or a push on the base branch. No AI attribution trailer is ever recorded — Akatsuki-Agent is the single admitted one. Runs on your own credentials — no App, no bot identity. From v0.7.0 Hatsu also runs on two more surfaces: the same skills and personas are generated into Codex and Cursor layouts under surfaces/ by nen surface mirror, placed into the repository you are standing in by the warm-up (.agents/skills/ plus an AGENTS.md persona appendix, or .cursor/skills/ plus .cursor/agents/) and excluded through .git/info/exclude rather than your .gitignore — invoked as $name on Codex and /name on Cursor, hatsu:name on Claude Code. Two absences are named rather than assumed: neither of those surfaces has a turn-end hook, so jutaisho rings the bell in-session and says so, and Codex has no in-session subagent, so hanten raises a reviewer as a second codex exec run in its own worktree. The model matrix carries a column per surface — the reviewer tier is deep everywhere, opus / sol / grok — Cursor is Cursor-native only, and the frontier tier never runs a subagent on any surface. docs/SURFACES.md is the authority; scripts/surface_mirror_check.sh fails a mirror that has drifted from its source. Hard dependency on the Nen CLI, checked at warm-up against nen/contract.json, failing closed with auto-install.
